claim: Keep gemma4-hvm:official-q4 as the provisional default, but do not claim a quality win over gemma4:e4b, gemma4:12b, or gemma4:26b. At num_predict=32 all four produced the same three calibration answer prefixes; warm-route latency is broadly overlapping. The e4b/12b/26b first cases were cold/model-switch loads, while official-q4 was already resident, so first-case latency comparisons are model-load-order confounded.
linchpin: Randomized, counterbalanced cold/warm repetitions with explicit unloads and semantic validators could reverse the latency ranking or expose quality differences.

claim: Reject 8; retain 16 as the concise-task frontier candidate and 32 as the safer default. num_predict=8 truncated the coding response, whereas 16/32/64 completed all three calibration cases. Held-out 16 and 32 both returned the same correct three answer prefixes. There is no demonstrated quality or latency benefit for 64 on this tiny suite.
linchpin: Longer or less constrained held-out tasks may require more than 16 tokens; only three held-out prompts were measured.

claim: Prefer p4-q8 for the measured 8-request direct-Ollama workload: all variants were 8/8 successful, and p4-q8 improved p50 versus p1-f16 (1003ms vs 1330ms) while p8-q8 worsened p50 to 1264ms; p8-q8 had the best measured tail (1267ms vs 1412ms and 2181ms). Treat p4-q8 versus p8-q8 as throughput/median versus tail tradeoff, not a universal winner.
linchpin: Repeated mixed-length HVM-route load may change the frontier; this comparison changes parallelism and KV type together and has one batch per cell.

claim: Preserve p8 as a scale candidate: prior still-available 60-way direct-Ollama evidence is 60/60 HTTP 200 with min=8545ms, p50=10855ms, p90=13215ms, max=14436ms, versus the other available 60-way run at p50=174216ms. This is supporting, not release-grade, evidence because the artifacts are ephemeral /tmp outputs and request-level semantic correctness was not validated.
linchpin: A reproducible checked-in 60-way HVM-route trace with response validators and fully recorded server settings is required before adopting p8 for production.

claim: Keep the request envelope and environment guardrails pinned: recorded oracle evidence reports 26/26 and rejection of invalid values before curl. Equivalent duplicate-key mutation is correctly classified as equivalent rather than killed. These are stubbed C/request-boundary tests, not live Ollama or end-to-end HVM-route serving tests.
linchpin: A live capture through the HVM route could reveal divergence between the stubbed curl boundary and actual Ollama behavior.

claim: Keep the lifecycle hardening: branch changes supervise owned Ollama, bound readiness, validate /api/version identity, propagate signal-derived status, and move prompts through an ephemeral file. Recorded lifecycle evidence is weaker/stale at 18/18 while the current harness declares 25 assertions, so rerun/current evidence is required. These are process-stub tests, not direct-Ollama serving or HVM-route generation tests.
linchpin: A clean current run of the 25-assertion harness plus a real owned-Ollama smoke test must confirm the documented behavior.

claim: Use the manifest harness for trace collection, not yet for model selection. It has immutable split/hash checks, records failures and HVM environment, and invokes run.sh (therefore calibration/held-out JSONL are HVM-route tests). But validators only establish manifest/invocation/exit/no-drop; they do not score semantic or exact-format correctness. The suite has only three prompts per split, single sequential runs, no randomized load order, and empty model_digest fields, so benchmark validity is insufficient for strong quality or latency rankings.
linchpin: Add per-case expected-output validators, repeated randomized/counterbalanced runs, cold/warm labels, and reliable model digest capture; then rerun held-out without tuning on it.
